```{r setup, include=FALSE}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(tibble)
  library(tidyr)
  library(readr)
  library(purrr)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(here)
  library(readxl)     # the clinical table is .xlsx
})

# The house style is sourced HERE, unconditionally and before opts_chunk$set:
# the figure defaults below call fig_width().
source(here("code", "plot_theme.R"))           # house figure style + fig_width()/label_n()
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.width = fig_width("double"), fig.height = fig_height("double"),
                      dev = c("png", "pdf"))   # PNG for the site, PDF exported to output/
source(here("code", "pdf_export.R"))

SLUG <- "paper_stare"
# WHICH ARMS THIS PAGE IS ABOUT. The STARE share carries the same two FlowPath gating
# sessions as before, re-run on STARE-registered slides (code/arms.R). The MAIN
# panels are Massimo2's gating; Massimo1's is the supplementary twin. They are never
# pooled: two gatings of the same cells, stacked, would count every cell twice.
ARM      <- "stare_massimo2"
ARM_SUPP <- "stare_massimo1"

# load_data.R brings dds, clinical_data, counts_data, expr_scales and ihc_for(). It
# stops when data/counts.RData or data/clinical_data.xlsx is missing, so it is
# caught here and the page says which input it lacks instead of failing to knit.
load_error <- NULL
have_data <- tryCatch({
  invisible(capture.output(suppressMessages(source(here("code", "load_data.R")))))
  source(here("code", "validation_helpers.R"))
  source(here("code", "paper_figures.R"))
  TRUE
}, error = function(e) { load_error <<- conditionMessage(e); FALSE })

# Each arm's cells are read once (ihc_for caches them) and every panel below is a
# cut of them. The gates are defined HERE so every gated chunk knows its input.
have_main <- have_data && nrow(ihc_for(ARM)) > 0
# The supplement reuses the main section's groups, RNA bridge and frame builder,
# so it is gated on the main arm too.
have_supp <- have_main && nrow(ihc_for(ARM_SUPP)) > 0
have_qs   <- have_main && requireNamespace("immunedeconv", quietly = TRUE)
```

This page builds every manuscript panel this repository feeds from the
**STARE data**, the study's main data since the 2026-10-23 export, in one place:

| panel | what it shows | built by |
|---|---|---|
| Fig 6(a), right | CD45⁺ cells, % of all cells, hot vs cold | `paper_immune_fraction_hotcold()` |
| Fig 6(b), bottom row | CD45⁺, CD3⁺, CD8⁺, CD4⁺, FOXP3⁺ % against bulk RNA of the matching gene(s) | `paper_rna_marker_scatter()` |
| Suppl. Fig S10 | FlowPath population fraction against quanTIseq | `paper_deconv_scatter()` |

The images in Fig 6(a) left and 6(b) top are microscope crops and are not made here.

**Where the cells come from.** `data/stare/` is the share's
`2026.10.23_STARE/csv/` directory: `Massimo1/<patient>.csv` and
`Massimo2/<patient>.csv` hold one FlowPath export per patient per gating session,
each covering the **whole slide**, and the two later patients sit at the top level
(`15370.csv`, `36766_2.csv`). No polygon is shipped. Which cells are inside the
tumour annotation is FlowPath's own call, carried in each file's
`Out_of_annotation` column, and every count on this page is over the cells it
marks inside. `36766_2.csv` is read as patient **36672-2**, the clinical sheet's
spelling (`STARE_FLAG_FILES` in `code/arms.R`).

```{r load-status, results = "asis"}
if (!have_data) {
  cat("**Inputs missing — nothing below is computed.** `code/load_data.R` stopped with:\n\n",
      "```\n", load_error, "\n```\n\n",
      "It needs `data/counts.RData` and `data/clinical_data.xlsx`.\n", sep = "")
} else {
  for (a in c(ARM, ARM_SUPP)) {
    st <- arm_tier_status(arm_spec(a))
    cat("- **`", a, "`**: ", nrow(ihc_for(a)), " cells read from `data/",
        arm_spec(a)$root, "/", arm_spec(a)$region_csv$dir, "/` and the csv-only files at `data/",
        arm_spec(a)$root, "/`", if (!any(st$exists)) " — **directory not found**" else "",
        "\n", sep = "")
  }
  if (!have_main)
    cat("\n**No cells for `", ARM, "`.** Link the share:\n\n",
        "```sh\nln -s /hpcnfs/techunits/imaging/work/ATTEND/2026.10.23_STARE/csv data/stare\n```\n",
        sep = "")
}
```

## Cells inside the annotation

Per patient: the cells in the export, how many `Out_of_annotation` marks inside,
and the rule that decided (`flag` for every STARE patient). Everything below
reads only the inside cells. The table makes a patient with almost nothing inside,
or 100% inside, visible before it turns up as an outlier in a figure.

```{r frames, eval = have_main}
# One frame set per arm: per-cell membership, the inside cells, and the union
# metrics row per patient (cd45_over_inside etc. — region_ratios_area() over the
# inside cells). arm_metrics() and arm_cells_in_annotation() both route STARE
# patients through arm_cut_by_flag(), so the two agree on every patient.
stare_frames <- function(arm) {
  spec   <- arm_spec(arm)
  cells  <- ihc_for(arm)
  scoped <- arm_cells_in_annotation(spec, cells)
  list(arm    = arm,
       scoped = scoped,
       inside = filter(scoped, in_annotation %in% TRUE),
       union  = arm_metrics(spec, cells, NULL, "union"))
}
main <- stare_frames(ARM)

knitr::kable(arm_in_annotation_inventory(main$scoped),
             caption = paste0("`", ARM, "`: cells per patient and how many the export ",
                              "flags inside the annotation."))
```

## The hot/cold axis

Hot and cold are the top and bottom **four** patients by the clinical `HOT score`
(`data/clinical_data.xlsx`), ranked among the patients with STARE cells. It is one
ranking, built once by `paper_hotcold_groups(k = 4)`, and every panel below groups
or colours by it. Fig 6 shows four cases a side; with eight patients, that puts
every patient in a group.

```{r hotcold, eval = have_main}
groups <- paper_hotcold_groups(clinical_data, patient_ids = main$union$patient_id,
                               source = "hot_score", k = 4)
knitr::kable(arrange(groups, group, desc(hot_score)),
             caption = "Hotscore groups, highest score first within each group.")
```

## Fig 6(a) — CD45⁺ cells, hot vs cold

y is `cd45_over_inside × 100`: CD45⁺ cells over all cells inside the annotation,
per patient, from the `stare_massimo2` exports. A cell counts as CD45⁺ when its
FlowPath phenotype falls in an immune lineage (`cell_lineage()`). The box shows
the group's median and quartiles, with every patient drawn on top. P is the
exact two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test. With four cases a side, a complete
separation gives the smallest P the design can reach, 2/70 = 0.029, so P = 0.029
means "the groups do not overlap" and nothing stronger.

```{r fig6a, eval = have_main, fig.width = panel_width(50), fig.height = panel_height(62)}
p6a <- paper_immune_fraction_hotcold(main$union, groups, test = "wilcoxon", percent = TRUE)
print(p6a)
```

```{r fig6a-numbers, eval = have_main}
knitr::kable(
  main$union |>
    transmute(patient_id, cd45_pct = 100 * cd45_over_inside, n_inside) |>
    left_join(select(groups, patient_id, group, hot_score), by = "patient_id") |>
    arrange(group, desc(cd45_pct)),
  digits = 1,
  caption = sprintf("Fig 6(a) values. Wilcoxon P = %.4f (%s).",
                    attr(p6a, "test")$p,
                    if (attr(p6a, "test")$exact) "exact" else "normal approximation, ties"))
```

## Fig 6(b), bottom row — imaging against bulk RNA

For each marker, y is the percentage of inside cells that FlowPath calls positive
for it (`ihc_marker_fraction()`: `marker_pos()`, an explicit positive sign, over all
inside cells). x is `log1p` of the bulk RNA expression from `data/counts.RData`,
DESeq2-normalised and averaged over the marker's gene(s) (the strip under each
marker lists them), matched to the slide through the clinical CRF crosswalk
(`crf_to_slide_map()`). r is Pearson's correlation on the axes as drawn, and
the line is its least-squares fit. Points are coloured by the hotscore group
above. The Spearman column in the table is the rank check on r: with eight
cases, one point can move r a long way.

```{r rna-paired, eval = have_main}
crf2slide <- crf_to_slide_map(clinical_data)
rna       <- rna_marker_expression(counts_data, crf2slide)

rna_pair_for <- function(fr) {
  ihc_marker_fraction(fr$inside) |>
    select(patient_id, ends_with("_posfrac")) |>
    pivot_longer(-patient_id, names_to = "marker", values_to = "ihc_posfrac") |>
    mutate(marker = sub("_posfrac$", "", marker)) |>
    inner_join(rna$expr, by = c("marker", "patient_id"))
}
rna_paired <- rna_pair_for(main)
FIG6_MARKERS <- c("CD45", "CD3", "CD8", "CD4", "FOXP3")

cat("patients with both STARE cells and bulk RNA:",
    n_distinct(rna_paired$patient_id), "\n")
if (length(rna$missing_genes))
  cat("mapped genes absent from the RNA matrix:", paste(rna$missing_genes, collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

```{r fig6b, eval = have_main, fig.width = fig_width("double"), fig.height = panel_height(52)}
p6b <- paper_rna_marker_scatter(rna_paired, groups, markers = FIG6_MARKERS,
                                genes = rna$genes)
print(p6b)
```

```{r fig6b-stats, eval = have_main}
knitr::kable(attr(p6b, "stats"), digits = 2,
             caption = "Fig 6(b): Pearson r (as printed in each panel) and Spearman rho, per marker.")
```

## Suppl. Fig S10 — FlowPath populations against quanTIseq

x is the share of all inside cells that FlowPath assigns to each population
(`ihc_comparison_fraction()`, gated as in Fig 5(a): CD8 T, CD4 T, Treg, NK). y is
quanTIseq's estimate for the matching cell type, from immunedeconv run on the
bulk RNA. Colour is the population and shape is the hotscore group. No fit line
is drawn, because the two axes have different denominators (cells counted vs. a
mixture estimate), so only the ranking is comparable.

**Expression scale.** quanTIseq asks for TPM. `data/counts.RData` carries no gene
lengths, so TPM cannot be derived from it, and this run uses the DESeq2-normalised
counts. Absolute fractions are therefore approximate, though the ranking across
patients, which is what the panel shows, is robust to that. Writing
`data/gene_lengths.tsv` (columns `gene`, `length`) switches the run to TPM with
no other change (`code/expression_scales.R`).

```{r quantiseq, eval = have_qs}
EXPR_SCALE <- if (!is.null(expr_scales$tpm)) "tpm" else "normalized"
expr_mat   <- expr_scales[[EXPR_SCALE]]
storage.mode(expr_mat) <- "double"

# quanTIseq and MCP-counter in ONE run on the same matrix, so the two S10 variants
# below differ only in the method.
DECONV_METHODS <- c("quantiseq", "mcp_counter")
deconv_long <- map_dfr(DECONV_METHODS, function(m)
  immunedeconv::deconvolute(expr_mat, m) |>
    pivot_longer(-cell_type, names_to = "sample", values_to = "score") |>
    mutate(method = m)) |>
  mutate(crf_id = norm_id(sample), patient_id = unname(crf2slide[crf_id])) |>
  filter(!is.na(patient_id))

qs_pair_for <- function(fr)
  deconv_lineage_scores(deconv_long) |> deconv_pair_with_ihc(ihc_comparison_fraction(fr$inside))
qs_paired <- qs_pair_for(main)
cat("deconvolution on the", EXPR_SCALE, "scale |",
    paste(DECONV_METHODS, collapse = " + "), "|",
    n_distinct(qs_paired$patient_id), "patients paired\n")
```

```{r figS10, eval = have_qs, fig.width = fig_width("oneandhalf"), fig.height = panel_height(90)}
pS10 <- paper_deconv_scatter(qs_paired, method = "quantiseq", groups = groups,
                             x_lab = "FlowPath fraction of all cells (inside annotation)")
print(pS10)
```

```{r figS10-stats, eval = have_qs}
knitr::kable(
  qs_paired |>
    filter(lineage %in% comparable_lineages) |>
    group_by(lineage) |>
    group_modify(~ paired_spearman(.x$ihc_frac, .x$score)) |>
    ungroup(),
  digits = 3, caption = "Suppl. S10: Spearman rho per population, FlowPath vs quanTIseq.")
```

## Suppl. S10, alternative — MCP-counter

MCP-counter fits the data as it is better than quanTIseq does. Each of its scores
is the mean log expression of one cell type's marker genes. A gene's length is the
same in every sample, so on the log scale it shifts every patient's score by the
same amount and the ranking across patients is unchanged. DESeq2-normalised counts
are therefore a valid input, which they are not for quanTIseq. The cost: its scores
are **arbitrary units per cell type**, comparable between patients but not between
populations, so it supports only a ranking claim (Spearman) and needs one panel per
population.

**Which populations it has.** Every cell type MCP-counter reports, and the FlowPath
population it is compared against (or why it is not):

```{r mcp-populations, eval = have_qs}
knitr::kable(
  deconv_population_table(deconv_long, "mcp_counter") |>
    transmute(`MCP-counter cell type` = cell_type,
              `imaging population`    = ifelse(is.na(lineage), "—",
                                               DECONV_POPULATION_LABELS[lineage]),
              `FlowPath gate`         = coalesce(ihc_gate, ""),
              `not compared because`  = coalesce(why, "")),
  caption = "MCP-counter's cell types against the FlowPath gating tree.")
```

**Layout A — one panel per population.** x is the FlowPath population as % of all
inside cells, y is the MCP-counter score, colour is the hotscore group, and each
panel prints its Spearman rho. No fit line is drawn, because a least-squares line
through arbitrary units would suggest a scale the method does not report.

```{r figS10-mcp, eval = have_qs, fig.width = fig_width("double"), fig.height = panel_height(52)}
pS10_mcp <- paper_deconv_facets(qs_paired, "mcp_counter", groups = groups)
print(pS10_mcp)
```

The same layout for quanTIseq, so the two methods can be compared panel for panel
(quanTIseq's y is a fraction of all cells):

```{r figS10-qs-facets, eval = have_qs, fig.width = fig_width("double"), fig.height = panel_height(52)}
print(paper_deconv_facets(qs_paired, "quantiseq", groups = groups,
                          lineages = c("CD8T", "CD4T", "Treg", "NK")))
```

**Layout B — agreement per population, both methods on one axis.** Each dot is the
Spearman rho between FlowPath and one method for one population, with the number of
patients beside it. With eight cases a rho moves about ±0.3 with a single patient,
so read differences between dots smaller than that as no difference.

```{r figS10-rho, eval = have_qs, fig.width = fig_width("oneandhalf"), fig.height = panel_height(70)}
# The populations a method choice turns on. quanTIseq's composites (CD4 any FOXP3,
# CD45+, CD45-) are sums of the leaves above and would repeat them.
S10_POPULATIONS <- c("T_total", "CD8T", "CD4T", "Treg", "NK", "Cytotoxic", "Stroma")
pS10_rho <- paper_deconv_rho_summary(qs_paired, methods = DECONV_METHODS,
                                     lineages = S10_POPULATIONS)
print(pS10_rho)
```

```{r figS10-rho-table, eval = have_qs}
knitr::kable(attr(pS10_rho, "stats") |>
               mutate(method = method_label(method),
                      population = DECONV_POPULATION_LABELS[lineage]) |>
               select(method, population, n, rho) |>
               arrange(population, method),
             digits = 2, caption = "Layout B's numbers.")
```

## Supplementary — the same panels on Massimo1's gating

The same three panels from `stare_massimo1`, the other gating session over the
same STARE cells, with the same hotscore groups. Comparing these with the panels
above shows how much the figure depends on where the gates were set. The two
arms are matched **by patient**. Their regions are not compared, because both cut
the same whole slide using their own flag.

```{r supp-frames, eval = have_supp}
supp <- stare_frames(ARM_SUPP)
knitr::kable(arm_in_annotation_inventory(supp$scoped),
             caption = paste0("`", ARM_SUPP, "`: cells per patient and how many are inside."))
```

```{r supp-fig6a, eval = have_supp, fig.width = panel_width(50), fig.height = panel_height(62)}
print(paper_immune_fraction_hotcold(supp$union, groups, test = "wilcoxon", percent = TRUE) +
        labs(title = "Massimo1 gating"))
```

```{r supp-fig6b, eval = have_supp, fig.width = fig_width("double"), fig.height = panel_height(52)}
p6b_supp <- paper_rna_marker_scatter(rna_pair_for(supp), groups, markers = FIG6_MARKERS,
                                     genes = rna$genes) +
  labs(title = "Massimo1 gating")
print(p6b_supp)
```

```{r supp-figS10, eval = have_supp, fig.width = fig_width("oneandhalf"), fig.height = panel_height(90)}
if (have_qs) {
  print(paper_deconv_scatter(qs_pair_for(supp), method = "quantiseq", groups = groups,
                             x_lab = "FlowPath fraction of all cells (inside annotation)") +
          labs(title = "Massimo1 gating"))
} else {
  cat("immunedeconv is not installed — no quanTIseq panel.\n")
}
```

Per patient, each marker's positive fraction under the two gatings, side by side.
A large difference here tells you the marker's gate, not the biology, decides
the panel.

```{r supp-gating-agreement, eval = have_supp}
gate_cmp <- full_join(
  rna_paired |> distinct(marker, patient_id, massimo2 = 100 * ihc_posfrac),
  rna_pair_for(supp) |> distinct(marker, patient_id, massimo1 = 100 * ihc_posfrac),
  by = c("marker", "patient_id")) |>
  filter(marker %in% FIG6_MARKERS) |>
  mutate(diff = massimo2 - massimo1)
knitr::kable(
  gate_cmp |>
    group_by(marker) |>
    summarise(n = n(), median_m2 = median(massimo2, na.rm = TRUE),
              median_m1 = median(massimo1, na.rm = TRUE),
              max_abs_diff = max(abs(diff), na.rm = TRUE),
              spearman = suppressWarnings(cor(massimo2, massimo1, method = "spearman",
                                              use = "complete.obs")),
              .groups = "drop") |>
    arrange(match(marker, FIG6_MARKERS)),
  digits = 2,
  caption = "Positive % per marker under each gating (medians over patients) and their per-patient agreement.")
```

## Exported numbers

Each plotted value is also written to `output/paper_stare/`, so a panel can be
redrawn or checked in Affinity without re-knitting.

```{r export-numbers, eval = have_main}
out <- here("output", "paper_stare")
dir.create(out, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
write_csv(left_join(transmute(main$union, patient_id, cd45_pct = 100 * cd45_over_inside),
                    groups, by = "patient_id"),
          file.path(out, "fig6a_cd45_hotcold.csv"))
write_csv(filter(rna_paired, marker %in% FIG6_MARKERS) |>
            mutate(ihc_pct = 100 * ihc_posfrac, log1p_rna = log1p(rna_expr)),
          file.path(out, "fig6b_marker_vs_rna.csv"))
if (exists("qs_paired")) write_csv(qs_paired, file.path(out, "figS10_deconv_pairs.csv"))
cat("written:", paste(list.files(out), collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

```{r export-pdfs, include=FALSE}
export_pdf_figures(SLUG)
```
